name: rasa.module.tasks
description: Portable task-management lifecycle, mountable into any domain or orchestrator. Seven directories are the state — triage, backlog, active, review, blocked, completed, closed — and there is no status: field to disagree with them. Every transition is one command that stamps the frontmatter, appends to the append-only tasks/history.tsv and moves the file. Ships two executables the project runs directly (.claude/bin/task, .claude/bin/check-tasks) so the lifecycle and the invariants that hold it are enforced rather than described. Domain-neutral by construction: the one varying concern — what 'done' requires — is delegated to the project-owned .claude/done-gate.md, and needs no version control to work.

rasa.note: The first module-kind Element. Mounts into a parent domain or orchestrator and installs a portable task lifecycle. The one domain-specific concern - what 'done' means - is delegated to a project-owned .claude/done-gate.md (seeded here, skip-if-exists); domains extend further via .claude/<domain>-task-rules.md. v1.0.0 is a clean break from 0.1.x: the frontmatter schema changed, the terminal transitions gained commands that perform them, and the substrate features 0.1.2/0.1.3 bolted on (the source clone, /sync, /promote, /whoami, the identity stamp, parent_kind tenant) were removed - they were a module claiming what its parent owns, and they cited canon amendment numbers that do not exist. A module claims only paths inside its own capability vocabulary: .claude/task-rules.md, .claude/task-templates/, the task/backlog/roadmap skills, .claude/bin/, .claude/done-gate.md and the tasks/ ledger. bin/migrate-tasks converts a 0.1.x ledger and is deliberately NOT installed - it is the one place allowed to read a version-control history, which is exactly why it must never reach content/.

element.description: Element-owned files mirrored into the install target per canon ELEMENT_CONTRACT.md §7. Refreshed on every Element upgrade, so nothing here may hold project state. The done-gate and the tasks/ ledger are NOT here - they are project-owned (see seed.files). Every file below is domain-neutral and is scanned for that by bin/check-manifest's hard-rule check before release.

files.note: The lifecycle spine: the seven directories, the transition set, the frontmatter contract, the id grammar, and the discipline around them. Element-owned; refreshed on upgrade. Names .claude/done-gate.md as the verification seam and .claude/<domain>-task-rules.md as the extension seam; it hardcodes neither's contents.

One body template per task type (change / defect / upkeep / inquiry / record), written by bin/task new. Element-owned; refreshed on upgrade. Depth is derived from whether ## Acceptance criteria holds a real checkbox, so there is no separate stub template and no depth field.

The three task skills: /task (drives the lifecycle through .claude/bin/task), /backlog and /roadmap (read + render). Only these three - a module must not claim a skill name outside its own capability vocabulary, which is how v0.1.2's /sync, /promote and /whoami silently overwrote the same-named skills of domain-code and domain-writer under directory-mirror.

The two executables the project runs: bin/task (the 12 lifecycle verbs, each one atomic command that writes the frontmatter, appends to tasks/history.tsv and performs the move) and bin/check-tasks (the validator - every invariant the spine states, mechanically). Element-owned; refreshed on upgrade. Pure standard library, no version control, no network: they must run in a project that has neither.

What this module ships and where each file lands. Fork/author-time documentation; policy opt-in means bin/init registers it and installs nothing. Its install table is generated from this manifest - see the bump ritual in CLAUDE.md.

seed.description: One-time, project-owned files copied at install only, per canon ELEMENT_CONTRACT.md §7. These belong to the consuming project the moment they land and are never overwritten by an Element upgrade - the project's done-gate, its task ledger, its config and its history. A re-init is non-destructive for every entry here.

files.note: The per-project verification contract - what review/ -> completed/ requires here. Project-owned; the domain fills it (a clinic writes clinical sign-off; a firm writes conflict check + partner approval; a novelist writes the continuity pass). Ships a minimum-honest default plus commented examples. This is the single file in the Element allowed to carry stack vocabulary, and bin/check-manifest allowlists it by name for exactly that reason.
Human orientation to tasks/: the seven directories, intake vs triage, the five always-required frontmatter keys, the two commands, and the pointer to the done-gate.
Pre-triage capture: prose with no ids, appended to over the life of the project. The only place in the ledger where something may be unstructured.

The phase registry. Every phase a task may name is a `## Phase <id> - <name>` heading here, and every phased task is listed under exactly one of them; bin/check-tasks proves the frontmatter and this file agree in both directions. Project-owned - the phases are the project's, not the Element's.

Optional project declarations: the target axis (platforms / matters / manuscripts) that makes the target field required, the actor and series allowlists, and migrated_on - the attribution ratchet date, stamped with {{TODAY}} at install so that unknown attributions can persist from before it and can never be created after it. A project that deletes this file is still fully valid.

The curated, append-only chronological record of meaningful actions (ships, milestones, rule changes, incidents). task-rules.md makes it mandatory; v0.1.x mandated it and shipped nothing, so consumers hit a missing file on their first ship. Project-owned.

The append-only transition log, seeded with its header row only. Written by bin/task, never by hand. It is simultaneously the audit trail a project without version control has never had, the corroboration for created / created_by / completed_by, and the id-retirement ledger that stops a deleted task's number from ever being reissued.

Stage directory scaffold (bin/init does not implement scaffold.directories, so the seven stages ship as seed placeholders). triage/: filed, has an id, uncommitted - the only stage where a phase is forbidden.
Stage directory scaffold. backlog/: phased, not started.
Stage directory scaffold. active/: in flight.

Stage directory scaffold. review/: the work is finished and the done-gate has not yet passed. New in v1.0.0, and the missing state that caused most of the 0.1.x drift - a partner's review, a clinical sign-off and a manuscript cooling-off read are all literally this.

Stage directory scaffold. blocked/: cannot proceed; enterable from backlog, active or review and returned by bin/task unblock to whichever of them it came from. Requires a non-empty ## Blocker section.
Stage directory scaffold. completed/: terminal, the done-gate passed. The count here is the number everyone reads, which is why work that ended WITHOUT being done goes to closed/ instead.

Stage directory scaffold. closed/: terminal, ended without being done - superseded, duplicate, obsolete or wont-do, each naming who closed it. New in v1.0.0; it is what keeps the completed/ count honest.

Stamped with the Element HEAD SHA at init. Lockfile shape per canon Spec §6 (Connection Contract). Written only when absent; an existing lockfile and its overrides[] survive a re-init. When this module is co-installed under a parent that also stamps a lockfile the parent's is authoritative (single-writer-per-path, Lock L-004); in the kernel pull model each Element gets its own holding folder, so there is no collision.

scaffold.description: Empty directories created at init by the declarative installer. bin/init does not implement scaffold.directories, so the seven stage directories ship as seed .gitkeep entries instead and this stays empty rather than declaring something nothing performs.
